documentation.sessionRemoval:
## Removing session data

The Session palette includes Remove Headers, Remove Cookies and Remove Storage alongside the Set nodes. Their config uses mode selected or all. In selected mode, click Add to create a row and enter one name/key in its input. Use that row's Delete button to remove it after confirmation. Editing rows does not remove browser data until the node runs. Switching to all hides the rows without discarding their values. Existing names load into separate inputs. In JSON, names remains a string of names/keys separated by escaped newlines, not a JSON list; variables are resolved before removing. All items must be selected explicitly. Missing entries are ignored.
- Remove Headers clears only extra context headers configured through Set Headers; names are case-insensitive. It cannot erase browser-generated headers or headers added by another override.
- Remove Cookies optionally narrows selected names by exact domain and path; empty filters apply to all domains/paths with those names. All mode clears cookies only in this isolated automation session.
- Remove Storage requires scope local or session and a prior Navigate to the intended origin. All clears only that storage; sessionStorage belongs to the current page.

Add example includes dedicated offline processes for selected and all removal, with checks of the resulting state.
documentation.validationVariants:
## Partial and negative checks

Assertion supports exists/not-exists, visible/not-visible, text-equals/text-not-equals, text-contains/text-not-contains, value-equals/value-not-equals, value-contains/value-not-contains, url-equals/url-not-equals, url-contains/url-not-contains, and response-status/response-status-not-equals. Use selector for element checks and expected for comparisons; status comparisons require a valid HTTP status. not-visible accepts hidden or absent elements; not-exists requires absence. Text/value comparisons still require an element.

Validate Data supports exists/not-exists, equals/not-equals, contains/not-contains, matches/not-matches and json-equals/json-not-equals for every data source. Contains uses a case-sensitive substring of the text representation, not exact equality. Regex operators require a valid regular expression; JSON operators require valid expected JSON and ignore object key order. Negative comparisons require a present, non-null value: use not-exists for a missing property, cookie or storage key. An empty string exists. These checks observe the current state; they do not delete or change it.

Add example includes Validation variants with a working example of every option. Use these flows as a starting point and adapt their selectors and expected values.

documentation.introduction:
# Browser Control Center {version} — {area}: usage context for an AI

Help me use Browser Control Center inside Visual Studio Code. This guide describes user features and the data the application accepts. I do not need changes to the extension's code.

WHAT THE APPLICATION DOES
- Manual prepares a browser session and applies values to web pages.
- Formulas stores JavaScript data generator functions. Arrays stores JSON lists from which a random item is selected. These global resources can be reused by Manual and Automations.
- Automations organizes groups and visual processes with connected nodes, variables, actions and checks.
- In Manage browser, choose installed Chrome or install/verify Managed Chromium. Manual, Automations and formula tests require an available browser. Arrays does not. Sessions are isolated from your personal profile; each automated process starts clean. Saving a configuration does not retain cookies from a closed session.

HOW TO HELP ME
1. Identify whether I need a Manual profile, formula, array or automation, and where I will paste the result.
2. If I am modifying something, ask for its View JSON document and preserve its IDs where appropriate. This generic guide does not include my current document, selectors or actual resource catalog.
3. Ask only for the missing data needed to run the case: URL, real CSS selectors, sample response or resource IDs. Do not present invented selectors or resources as verified. You may offer a clearly identified, self-contained example.
4. When I request JSON to paste, return one valid JSON document without comments, trailing commas, ellipses or explanations inside it. Escape newlines, quotes and string backslashes. true/false and null are unquoted. Code, storage values or a body may require JSON inside an escaped string.
5. Outside the document, briefly explain where to paste it, which button to click and which values to replace. Do not promise a flow works against a website whose selectors we do not know.

PASTING, IMPORTING AND SAVING
- Auto-save is enabled when a document has no saved preference. A saved autoSaveEnabled: false is respected; opening or updating the extension does not enable it again.
- Manual, Arrays, Formulas and Automations have an Auto-save switch at the very top, above the title. It is enabled by default and saves changes after 5 seconds of inactivity. Each interaction restarts the wait. It does not apply fields, test formulas or run flows.
- Only interactions with extension controls count: typing or using the keyboard in a field, clicking buttons or other controls, and dragging items. Moving the mouse, hovering over a field, scrolling or clicking the background does not restart the wait. During a drag, the 5 seconds start when you release the item.
- The preference travels in JSON as preferences: {autoSaveEnabled: true|false}, inside profile for Manual, each Arrays/Formulas resource, and the Automations document. It is optional: older documents remain valid. Disabling it cancels the pending wait; click Save to persist the disabled setting. Auto-save pauses while editing View JSON or deciding what to do with unsaved changes; only valid data is saved. A failure preserves the draft without continuous retries, and save acknowledgements preserve edits made after sending.
- View JSON → replace the complete document → Apply changes → Save. Apply changes loads a draft; it does not execute or save it. Do not paste a loose node list or only the data field into View JSON.
- Import opens a .json file; for chat content, save it in a file or use View JSON on an item you have already created/selected.
- Formulas and Arrays: View JSON represents exactly one resource inside data, a list of length 1. An import file may contain several resources.
- Manual: data is a bundle with bundleVersion, profile, formulas and arrays. Automations: data is a document with groups.
- All complete documents use format, schemaVersion: 1, extensionVersion: "{version}", exportedAt (ISO date or null) and data. Internal object versions are independent: Manual profile 2; Manual bundle 1; formula/array 1; automation document {automationSchemaVersion}.
- For Manual profiles and Formulas/Arrays resources, View JSON requires the open item's ID to be preserved. To use a new example from this guide, import it as a file or replace its ID with the open draft's ID. Use unique IDs and descriptive names. Import resolves collisions without silently overwriting; the same ID with identical content may be reused.
- Documents support up to 100 MiB, with a warning at 80%. Save/Discard/Cancel protects changes when switching selection; closing the tab may lose a draft. Export lets you keep a copy.
- If an action fails, check Output → Browser Automation and share the relevant message. Automated runs open that panel.
documentation.sessionReference:
## Session data reference (Manual and session nodes)

Each row has a unique id and a boolean enabled; disabled rows are not applied.
- Query parameter or header: {id, key, value, enabled}; key and value are strings. Parameters are built from enabled rows: any query string in the base URL is removed and replaced. Add multiple rows to repeat a key.
- Cookie: {id, name, value, domain, path, expires, secure, httpOnly, sameSite, enabled}. name/value/domain/path are strings, expires is null or an ISO date; secure/httpOnly are booleans; sameSite is Strict, Lax or None. domain has no https:// or path. With an empty domain, the active URL is used, so navigate first. path is usually /. SameSite None usually requires secure true.
- Storage: {id, key, value, valueType, enabled}. value is ALWAYS a string; valueType is string, number, boolean, json or null. Examples: value "42" with number; "false" with boolean; "{\"role\":\"tester\"}" with json; "null" with null. Navigate to the origin before writing storage. localStorage belongs to the origin; sessionStorage also depends on the tab.
- Override: {id, matcherType, matcher, method, action, status, headers, body, contentType, enabled}. matcherType: exact, glob or regex; matcher is the pattern as text; method: ANY, GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD or OPTIONS. action fulfill responds with an integer status 100–599, string body, string contentType and headers (header rows); abort cancels; continue-modified continues with modified headers and body. To intercept a URL with a query string, use an appropriate glob or include the query in an exact match. Install rules before triggering the request. A JSON body is stored as an escaped string. New rules replace the active rule list rather than accumulating as independent nodes.
- Viewport: {preset, width, height, deviceScaleFactor, hasTouch, isMobile}. width/height are positive integers; scale is positive and the last two fields are booleans. Presets: desktop (1920×1080), laptop (1366×768), tabletPortrait (768×1024), tabletLandscape (1024×768), mobilePortrait (390×844), mobileLandscape (844×390) or custom. Include all fields even with a preset. Use custom for your own dimensions.
- CSS selectors: prefer #id or stable attributes such as [data-testid="email"]. Select captures an element from the visible Manual browser, which must be open. Escape cancels. Selectors traverse open Shadow DOM; do not assume support for closed roots or every iframe. In Automations, selector-based reads and writes use the first match.
documentation.resourceReference:
## Reusable resources

Formula: {schemaVersion:1, id, name, code, createdAt, updatedAt}. Array: {schemaVersion:1, id, name, items, createdAt, updatedAt}. IDs, names, code and dates are strings; dates use ISO format; items is a list of JSON values. Saved resource names must be unique, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace.
A formula declares function generate() with no parameters (async is also supported). It returns text, a finite number, boolean, JSON object/list, null or undefined. undefined means no result and cannot fill a field. It runs in isolation without network, Node or VS Code APIs, with a 2-second timeout: it cannot read the DOM of the page I am automating or receive process variables. Use Save Data to read the DOM. Do not use imports or external packages.
An array contains JSON values; each use randomly chooses one. It does not iterate through the list or guarantee distinct values. An empty array produces no result.
Manual can carry its resources inside the bundle's formulas and arrays. Automations only stores resourceId: import/save resources in their own pages first and use their actual IDs; do not add an invented catalog to an automation document.
documentation.manual:
{introduction}
## Using Manual

1. Select a profile or click New and give it a name. Save it to retain the configuration. New does not create a browser session by itself.
2. Configure the viewport before Start. Start creates a clean session; Open starts one if needed and navigates to the URL built with query parameters. If you change the viewport of an open session, use Apply with clean restart; the current session state will be lost.
3. Tab buttons change the active page. Headers and cookies affect the context; storage and fields apply to the active page.
4. Editing or saving a profile does not automatically apply all headers, cookies, storage or fields. Use Apply per row or Apply all in the corresponding section. To change subsequent requests, apply headers/overrides before navigating or trigger the request again. Overrides also synchronize when their configuration changes while a session is open.
5. Navigate before applying storage, fields or cookies without a domain. Open the website, select each target and use Generate sample to check the value source before Apply.
6. Reset in the fields section restores values captured before applying during the current session; it does not clear the profile or browser.
7. Stop attempts a normal close, Force close terminates an unresponsive browser, and Clean restart creates a session without previous cookies/storage. Save keeps profile configuration, not a live authenticated session.
8. Import/Export carries the profile and its referenced resources. View JSON lets you edit the bundle without a file. Apply changes preserves profile.id and loads the draft; use Save or Auto-save to persist it. Formulas are reused by equivalent code, and arrays by equivalent content, when resolving a bundle.
9. Auto-save is at the very top, above the title. It is enabled by default and can be toggled per profile. When enabled, it saves changes after 5 seconds without user activity in Manual; each new interaction restarts the wait. It does not apply data to the browser. If disabled, click Save to retain that preference. It pauses while editing View JSON or deciding what to do with unsaved changes. Applying JSON schedules it again. Errors preserve the draft without continuous retries; edits made during a save are not overwritten.

## Applying values explicitly

- Inputs / Generators, Cookies and Request Overrides show a single Apply button per row. Expanded: in its actions area. Collapsed: next to the summary. You do not need to expand a row to apply it.
- Sections have distinct icons and headers with item counts. In Cookies, Request Overrides and Inputs / Generators, Expand all and Collapse all affect only that group's rows. Individual and group expansion updates each row's expanded preference in the draft, retained by Save or Auto-save and included in View JSON/Export/Import. This does not apply browser data; controls are disabled for empty lists.
- Reorder rows using the dotted handle: query parameters, headers, cookies, both storages, overrides, each override's headers, and generators. Drag within the same list; sections do not move and groups do not mix. Alt+↑/↓ on a handle reorders with the keyboard. IDs, values and expansion are preserved. The new order is a draft change: Save retains it and View JSON/Export reflects it. Reordering does not apply data. Apply all follows generator order; the first enabled matching override takes priority.
- Inputs are filled only by Apply or Apply all. Loading, editing, selecting, importing or saving a profile, receiving browser state, starting/restarting or navigating does not trigger generators. Generate sample only previews a result; Reset restores originals through an explicit action.
- Apply all attempts every enabled row in order, even if another fails to generate or write. A final notice reports successful fields and failures. It does not undo successful fields or delete failed configurations. Empty arrays and formulas returning undefined mean no result and do not empty the input.
- Inputs / Generators notices appear in Manual without automatically opening Output, including element selection, sample generation and reset. Details remain available in Output → Browser Automation.
- If a selector finds no element, that row fails without waiting to fill it later. Navigate to the right page and click Apply again when the element is ready. Errors do not trigger automatic form execution.
- Manual typing temporarily blocks form submission during application, including submit/requestSubmit and Enter outside a textarea. After it finishes, the page's button or keyboard can submit manually. Textareas may contain newlines.
- Updating the extension under the same identity preserves saved profiles and resources. These features do not change profile schema v2 or require JSON migration. Save drafts before updating; a live browser session is not preserved.

## Manual document shape

When reordering, use the mouse wheel without releasing the handle to scroll the page or a scrollable list. The target updates as you scroll. Escape cancels; Auto-save waits until release.

format: browser-control-center/manual-profile.
data: {bundleVersion:1, profile:{...}, formulas:[...], arrays:[...]}.
profile: {schemaVersion:2, id, name, url, queryParams, headers, cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, requestOverrides, generatorBindings, viewport, createdAt, updatedAt}.
All collections must exist even when empty []. id/name/url/dates are strings. Preserve profile.id in View JSON. Do not confuse profile.schemaVersion:2 with the outer document's schemaVersion:1.
Optionally, profile.preferences is {autoSaveEnabled: true|false}; if absent, Auto-save is enabled. Rows in cookies, requestOverrides and generatorBindings accept expanded: true|false to retain their visual preference. If absent, cookies start closed and overrides/generators open. These preferences do not change application behavior or require a new schemaVersion.

## Manual fields and generators

Each generatorBinding is {id, generatorType, selector, propertyKind, propertyName, min, max, resourceId, literalValue, inputMode, delayMs, enabled}.
- generatorType: string (fixed text using literalValue), firstName, lastName, email, phone, number, dni, nie, cif, formula or array.
- selector: target CSS selector. propertyKind: value, textContent, innerText, checked, attribute or property. For attribute/property, propertyName is the name (e.g. data-id). Otherwise it may be "".
- value fills input/textarea. checked changes a checkbox; use a formula/array returning a boolean or fixed text "true"/"false". fill does not select a select option: to change its value property, use propertyKind property and propertyName value, or a sequence of Click nodes in Automations.
- min/max are numeric strings for number (including decimals for that precision); min must be less than or equal to max. Built-in numeric generators produce text. For other generators, keep e.g. min "0", max "100".
- resourceId is null for built-in generators; formula/array requires a catalog or portable bundle resource ID. Do not replace it with a name.
- literalValue is the fixed text. inputMode instant writes at once, and sequential simulates keys with numeric delayMs ≥0; it applies to propertyKind value. enabled disables a row without deleting it.
- Manual does not interpolate Automations variables: {itemId} here is literal text. Its formulas do not receive the profile as a parameter.
- Selecting sequential typing defaults to 100 ms per key; you can change it. Loading a profile preserves saved delays; switching modes preserves custom nonzero values.

{sessionReference}
{resourceReference}
## Complete example: local page with name, email and city

The document installs a page through an override: no server or Internet access is needed. Import it as a file or adapt profile.id to the ID in View JSON. Save, start the session, apply overrides if they are not synchronized yet, click Open, then Apply all under Inputs / Generators. The name is Ada; email and city come from the included resources.
{example}
## Helping with my case

Ask for the base URL, parameters, current View JSON document and target selectors. Clarify whether I need to apply values once (Manual) or chain steps with checks (Automations). Return the complete bundle preserving my profile ID, including new referenced resources and retaining existing sections unless I ask to remove them.
documentation.formulas:
{introduction}
## Using Formulas

1. Add creates a formula in the editor; choose a unique name. The list lets you switch formulas or select several to delete with confirmation.
2. In Code, write JavaScript declaring function generate() with no parameters. async function generate() is also supported. Do not paste an import JSON document here: this field contains JavaScript code only.
3. Generate example loads sample code into a draft; it does not run it. Auto-save may save the draft if enabled.
4. Test runs the current code even when unsaved and displays the value, type, duration or error. Save retains the formula so it appears in Manual and the Field node in Automations.
5. Export and View JSON contain exactly the selected formula in a one-item data list. Import accepts several formulas. Deleting a formula may leave unavailable references in profiles or flows that used it.
6. To paste an AI response into View JSON, preserve the open formula's id; click Apply changes, then Save. For code only, paste into Code and test before saving.
7. The Auto-save switch is at the very top. Enabled by default, it is a per-formula preference included as preferences: {autoSaveEnabled: true|false}. It saves after 5 seconds of inactivity with Save's validations and never runs code automatically. Failures preserve the code in the editor.

## Formula contract and limits

- Declare function generate() or async function generate(), without parameters. An arrow function alone is insufficient; the function must have this name and does not need export.
- Return JSON values (string, finite number, boolean, object, array or null) or undefined. undefined means No result; avoid it if the next step needs to fill a field.
- Promises are resolved. A throw or rejected promise fails. Waiting/looping for more than 2 seconds terminates the isolated execution.
- Execution uses a disposable headless page without network, requests or WebSockets; Node, require, filesystem, VS Code APIs, imports and external libraries are unavailable.
- No arguments or automation context are provided. The formula cannot inspect the visible browser DOM or an HTTP response from another session; use Save Data in Automations instead.
- Test data can use Math.random(), Date, strings, lists and ordinary JavaScript objects. Do not return BigInt, functions, cycles, instances that cannot be represented as JSON, or non-finite numbers.
- Each use runs generate again; do not assume shared state or unique values. A Field source may convert its JSON result to text when entering it.

{resourceReference}
## Complete document for View JSON or Import

format: browser-control-center/formulas. data is a list. Each formula requires schemaVersion:1, id, name, code, createdAt and updatedAt; code is a string containing JavaScript with escaped newlines.
For View JSON, replace the example ID with the open formula's ID. To create one from a file, use a new unique ID.
{example}
## Code examples for the Code editor (not JSON documents)

Fixed text: function generate() { return "Ada"; }
Number: function generate() { return Math.floor(Math.random() * 100) + 1; }
Checkbox: function generate() { return true; }
Object: function generate() { return {name:"Ada", role:"tester"}; }
Asynchronous without network: async function generate() { return await Promise.resolve({ok:true}); }

## Using a saved formula

In Manual, add a field/generator, choose Formula, select the resource and target element; Generate sample previews the value and Apply writes it. In Automations, create Field, choose Formula as its source, select the resource and CSS selector. In JSON, use generatorType formula and the actual resource ID in resourceId, not its name. A portable Manual profile can include it in data.formulas; an automation document does not import formulas itself.

For a custom formula, ask what type I need and which restrictions its value must satisfy. Return only code for Code or a complete document for View JSON, as requested. For objects stored as JSON text in an input, clarify whether to return the object or a JSON string.
documentation.arrays:
{introduction}
## Using Arrays

1. Add creates an array; give it a unique name. In JSON content, paste ONLY a JSON list, e.g. ["Madrid","Sevilla"]. Do not paste a document with format and data there.
2. Validate checks the content and reports the item count; it does not save. The root must be an array, not an object or JavaScript.
3. Test randomly chooses an item from the current content, even when unsaved, and displays its value and type. Each click makes a new selection.
4. Save requires valid content and makes the array available in Manual and Automations. Export and View JSON use the validated current content; it need not have been saved first.
5. The side list changes the active resource; its checkboxes allow Delete selected with confirmation. Deletion may leave unavailable references in profiles or flows.
6. In View JSON, preserve the open array's ID and exactly one resource in data. Apply changes loads the draft; click Save afterward. Import from file accepts multiple resources.
7. The Auto-save switch is at the very top. It is enabled by default, belongs to the current array and is included as preferences: {autoSaveEnabled: true|false}. It does not save invalid JSON content; correcting it restarts the 5-second wait. It does not select random items by itself.

## Accepted values and behavior

items may contain strings, finite numbers, true/false, null, objects and nested JSON lists. Comments, unquoted keys, trailing commas, undefined, NaN, Infinity, functions and JavaScript code are rejected. You may mix types, though a homogeneous list is usually more useful for a single field.
No JavaScript is executed. An array is not a loop or a sequence of steps: each use selects ONE random item, possibly repeating it. Empty arrays return No result; avoid them when a value is required to fill a field.
Use Formulas to generate new values. Use Automations for a sequence of actions. A selected object can be reused as JSON, or Save Data can extract a property from Field's output for later use.

{resourceReference}
## Option A: content for the JSON content editor
{items}
## Option B: complete document for View JSON or Import

format: browser-control-center/arrays. data is a list of resources; each resource contains schemaVersion:1, id, name, items, createdAt and updatedAt. items is an actual JSON list, not a string containing a list. For View JSON, replace the example ID with the open array's ID; use a unique ID to import a new one.
{example}
## Reusing the array

Save it first. In Manual, create a field/generator, choose Array and select it; specify the selector and property, then use Generate sample/Apply. In Automations, use Field with generatorType array and the actual ID as resourceId. An object or list is represented as JSON when written to an input; if you need a property, add Save Data with source previous and a path such as user.email, then reuse the variable in another Field.
Manual exports referenced arrays in data.arrays. Automations only keeps the reference, so import/save the array separately before running the flow.

For custom data, ask how many examples and which types I need, their required fields, and whether I want literal values or dynamic generation. Return only the list for JSON content, or the complete document for View JSON/Import, depending on the destination.
documentation.automations:
{introduction}
## Using Automations

1. Create a group and a process/flow inside it. Select the process in the tree. A group organizes processes; it is not an executable node inside another flow.
2. Configure its name, viewport and initial variables (a JSON object). Add nodes from the palette, configure each in the inspector and connect its right output to the next node's input.
3. The visual element picker uses the visible Manual browser: open an equivalent page there, click Select and capture an element. Execution uses a different, clean session, so include Navigate and any required access steps.
4. Run process follows dependencies; Run group attempts processes sequentially, each with its own clean browser and variables. Sessions are not shared with Manual or between processes. A node failure stops its process and skips remaining nodes; subsequent group processes are still attempted.
5. Pause acts between nodes; Continue resumes. Stop requests cancellation/normal shutdown; Force stop forces shutdown. Pause / Wait User offers Continue, Retry or Stop in both VS Code and the browser bar. The browser closes when a process finishes, except while waiting for manual intervention.
6. Output → Browser Automation reports each node's start, duration and failure, plus an execution summary. Cards show their states. For a failed field, check the selector, previous navigation, value type, resource availability and timeout.
7. Save/View JSON/Export accept drafts with incomplete nodes. Run, Import and Apply changes require valid configurations. Do not present an incomplete document as ready to run.
8. Add example creates self-contained offline processes for the application's features, including Save Data, plus an All connected flow. It adds a new group without replacing existing ones. Intentional manual pauses require Continue.

## Where to paste JSON and editing scope

The side list shows Group headers with counts and indented processes labeled Process with their status. Rename a group or process directly in the list or in the wide Group name / Process name editor fields. Adding a process selects its temporary name so you can replace it. Save or Auto-save retains names in JSON; renaming does not change IDs or run processes.

Dotted handles let you drag entire groups, reorder processes within a group or move them between groups. Dropping a process on another inserts it before/after according to the indicator; dropping on a group's header or list space appends it, even when empty or collapsed. IDs, nodes, edges and variables are unchanged. Alt+↑/↓ on a handle reorders within its list. The header arrow collapses/expands the group while keeping actions visible; it does not disable processes. Adding a process expands the group to edit its name. Save or Auto-save retains order and expansion, including in JSON; group execution follows process order, but dragging/collapsing executes nothing.

Auto-save is at the very top and enabled by default. It saves the complete groups document after 5 seconds of inactivity, using Save's draft validations, and runs no processes. The document preference is preferences: {autoSaveEnabled: true|false}, also when exporting a selection. Applying selection JSON that includes preferences updates it; if omitted, the current preference is preserved. Import adds groups and keeps the destination document's preference.

Select a group or process and click View JSON. For a selected process, data.groups must contain exactly one group with exactly one process; for a selected group, it must contain exactly one group, which may include several processes. The result applies to that selection and preserves its identity; other selections are not replaced. Preserve copied IDs and keep every connection consistent. Do not paste multiple groups into this dialog.
Apply changes validates and returns to the canvas as a draft; click Save to persist. To add new groups rather than replace the selection, save the complete document to a file and Import. Import documents may contain multiple groups; collisions are resolved without silent overwrites. Export also uses the selected group/process.

## Exact JSON structure

Use the mouse wheel while holding a group/process handle to scroll the page or side list; the indicator and target update as you scroll. Escape cancels without reordering. Auto-save waits until release.

format: browser-control-center/automations; data is {schemaVersion:{automationSchemaVersion}, id, name, groups, createdAt, updatedAt}. Supported version 1 documents are upgraded automatically; keep their IDs and configuration.
Each group is {id, name, processes:[...]}.
Each group may include boolean expanded: true shows its list and false collapses it. If absent, it starts open; do not change schemaVersion. This preference survives import/export and save. Applying group JSON without it preserves the current preference.
Each process is {id, name, viewport, nodes:[...], edges:[...], variables:{...}}.
Each node is {id, type, position:{x,y}, config:{...}, timeoutMs:null}. x/y are finite canvas coordinates; timeoutMs null uses the default, or specify positive milliseconds. Do not replace type with its visible title: Field uses fill; Save Data uses capture-value.
Each edge is {id, sourceNodeId, sourcePort:"out", targetNodeId, targetPort:"in"}. Referenced node IDs must exist in the same process. Use unique IDs for documents, groups, processes, nodes and edges. Include empty lists where needed, nonempty names and ISO dates. Do not invent fields for loops, conditions or custom functions: no such nodes exist.
The graph rejects cycles and self-connections. Execution follows dependencies and does not draw a route by itself: connect steps that must be consecutive. Independent branches are ordered by vertical/horizontal node position, not by the nodes array; avoid relying on that incidental order.

## Variables, capture and types

- variables holds initial process values. Valid names begin with A–Z/a–z or underscore, followed by letters, digits or underscore. Do not use spaces, hyphens or dots; e.g. itemId.
- To store a variable, enter itemId without braces as the output name; to read it, use {itemId} in a configuration field. A string exactly equal to {itemId} preserves its JSON type; in "ID: {itemId}" it interpolates as text. Do not use dollar template syntax or {user.id} access: first extract the property into another variable.
- Set Variable stores a value, Extract Value reads the DOM, and Save Data accepts source dom or previous. Variables are also resolved inside configuration lists/objects. Referencing a missing variable fails. Variables are not persisted or passed to the next process.
- Save Data with source previous requires exactly one connected predecessor that produces data. Field (written value), Extract Value, Set Variable, Save Data, Generate Value and Wait with kind response produce data. Click, Navigate, validations and other waits do not. It does not automatically capture an HTTP response caused by Click.
- To capture an input: source dom, selector #name, property value, path "", valueType string and outputVariable savedName. For visible text, use innerText; full text, textContent; attributes, property attribute with the name in attribute. You can read value from input, textarea and select, although Field uses fill and does not select options.
- For JSON visible in #payload: source dom, property textContent, path item.id, valueType number. For a Wait response: source previous and path body.item.id. Use path "" to save the complete output.
- Paths use dots and array indices, e.g. body.items.0.id; not JSONPath, $, brackets or wildcards. JSON text can be traversed. Missing paths fail. Missing DOM attributes return null.
- valueType auto preserves the type (ordinary DOM reads are text); string converts to text; number requires a valid nonempty number; boolean accepts true/false; json parses complete JSON; null accepts an empty value or null. The path is applied before conversion. Objects and arrays written to inputs become JSON text.
- For network data, Wait response listens for future responses: arrange for it to be active when the response arrives. A Click whose response arrives before the following Wait can cause a timeout. If the response already arrived, Validate Data can validate observed data but cannot store it in variables. Do not promise a fixed delay retrieves past responses; capture a DOM result or use an example with a controlled response delay.
- Request Override modifies responses to actual browser requests, but sends no requests itself. There is no independent HTTP client node or node for arbitrary page JavaScript.

{sessionReference}
{resourceReference}
## Node catalog and valid reference configurations

Each block below is ONLY the specified node's config object, not a document to paste into View JSON. Use it inside a complete node with its type. For headers, cookies and storage, fill entries with the rows described above. Adapt examples to the actual page and retain required fields even when unused in a particular mode.
{nodeCatalog}
### Validate Data details

source request exposes url, method, headers and body; response exposes url, status, headers and body; cookie exposes value, domain, path, expires, httpOnly, secure, sameSite; localStorage/sessionStorage expose the key's value. Use urlPattern to narrow the last observed request/response (only the most recent 200 of each are retained). Use lowercase header names, e.g. headers.content-type.
pathPreset custom uses path. For presets, request accepts url, method, headers.content-type, headers.authorization or body; response accepts url, status, headers.content-type or body; cookie accepts the listed properties; storage uses "" for the complete value. With any non-custom preset, path does not override the preset.
expected is always a string. equals compares text representations; json-equals compares JSON independent of key order; matches uses a valid regular expression. exists/not-exists do not need expected and consider undefined or null absent. A custom request/response path such as body.user.id parses a JSON body when traversing it. For JSON in storage, use the actual key and an appropriate internal path.

## Complete import example: capture a field and JSON in the DOM

This example installs HTML through Request Override before navigation, writes Ada into #name, captures it as savedName, copies it to #copy and checks it. It then reads item.id from JSON in #payload as a number, stores itemId, writes "ID: 42" and checks it. It needs no Internet, login or global resources. Import the file to add the group, or paste into View JSON on a target group/process and save. The browser closes at the end; add Pause / Wait User before the end if you want to inspect it.
{example}
## Building my flow

Ask for the current selection's JSON, goal, URL, selectors and relevant sample data. For each Formula/Array reference, request a saved resource ID or prepare its separate document and explain import order. Include session setup, navigation, necessary waits and useful checks alongside field entry steps. Return a complete valid document for the selected scope, explaining where to paste it and any remaining external requirements.
extension.description: Control your browser, prepare test data and automate web workflows from VS Code.
examples.heading: Local Automations example
examples.description: This page and its API are served by a
examples.name: Name
migration.invalidDocument: The {schema} document must be a JSON object.
migration.invalidVersion: The {schema} document has an invalid or unsupported schemaVersion.
migration.futureVersion: The {schema} document uses schemaVersion {version}, newer than the supported version {current}. Update the extension to open it.
documentation.savedData:
## Saved data and extension updates

Saved profiles, formulas, arrays and automations are retained when updating the same extension installation. Supported older data is upgraded automatically when opened or imported. Keep the schema versions shown by View JSON or the current examples; do not change a version number to bypass an error. extensionVersion identifies the release that exported a document and is independent of schemaVersion.

Profile and resource selectors omit entries whose saved files no longer exist; an entry's name alone cannot recover its contents. If a resource is missing, import a backup or save it in its own page, then use its actual ID in dependent fields. Do not invent resource IDs or recreate a missing profile from an empty document unless I explicitly request a new profile.

If opening or upgrading saved data fails, its original file is not overwritten. Keep a backup and share the error; for an unsupported newer schema, update the extension instead of lowering schemaVersion. Save or export drafts before updating. Live browser sessions are not saved with the configuration.
documentation.browserSelection:
## Choosing the active browser

Open Manage browser and check Active browser; it reflects the saved selection. Choose Managed Chromium or installed Google Chrome, then use Verify selected to check availability. Changing the provider closes any active Manual browser session before applying the selection. Save your configuration first; the new session will not retain the old session's cookies or storage. Opening this panel or selecting a provider does not fill fields or run an automation.
documentation.resourceNavigation:
### Switching formulas and arrays

Opening a saved resource or an untouched new draft does not require saving before switching to another resource. A new draft shows Not saved yet until it is explicitly saved or edited and auto-saved. The Save/Discard/Cancel dialog appears only after actual edits, including changes made in View JSON. Saving updates the comparison baseline; any edits made while that save is in progress remain protected. Opening a page or selecting list checkboxes does not auto-save an untouched draft.
documentation.processCards: To view a process, click its card background or its Process label, not just its name field. You can also focus the card and press Enter or Space. Its action buttons, name field, move selector and drag handle keep their own behavior; selecting a card does not execute or modify the process.
